Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 23; the portal cover sheet is PDF page 1). A UK top-down and subsector study; most technology numbers are reprinted from other sources or are analysis assumptions, flagged in the notes. Main file (21 examples): Table 7-3 capacity-weighted SEC of the five UK cement kiln types (semi-wet, semi-dry Lepol, dry 4-stage, dry 4-stage precalciner, dry 5-stage precalciner; Moore 2011 data), BAT kiln 2.9-3.3 GJ/t, Khurana et al. (2002) Indian plant (3.7 GJ/t, 50% efficiency), fluidised bed kiln (3.4-0.42 GJ/t derived, demonstration), heat pumps (food and drink COP 4.38 at 80 degC; malting COP 4.3, 0.5-2.1 MWth), absorption chillers (single effect COP 0.7, double effect 1.0, min 350 kW) and heat transformer (COP 0.45-0.48), CHP assumptions (Table 3-6: 75% overall, heat-to-power 2:1, min 40 kWe), boiler efficiency 55-85% and 80% assumed, cement CCS 90-95% plant-level capture (share-to-capture). _flows: electrical output of cement waste-heat-to-power per kg clinker (Table 7-4, four sources). _measures: motor-system savings (Table 3-5), steam-system savings, kiln switch to BAT per kiln type (Table 7-3), fluidised bed kiln, precalciner payback, heat-to-power paybacks, clinker substitution, heat pumps per PJ heat, energy management. _other-values: kiln-type aggregate UK capacities, UK cement sector 2010 statistics, Khurana hot streams (Table 7-2) and electricity per t cement, heat pump limits and food-and-drink surplus heat (Table 7-1), ORC limits, CHP capacity statistics. Not loaded: Chapters 2, 4 and 5 (exergy method, policy, decomposition), NAP database sector results, Fig. 6-3 heat-to-power efficiencies (chart only), Appendix 6 paper reproductions (not included in the online copy). No costs other than paybacks are printed. Traps: kiln SECs are operating averages at 61% sector load; the kiln capacities in Table 7-3 are UK totals per kiln type (only the semi-wet one is a single kiln); COPs are calculated (55% of Carnot), not measured; the coke-oven GHG factor unit (tCO2e/MJ) is printed wrongly.
